criteria.criterion: A run test (cargo test -p athena-core) where the producer's first candidate touches a path governed by a decision in the base docs/decision-links.toml and adds no log entry or link shows the producer invoked a second time with a send-back brief that contains the gate's message (GATE_REASON_PREFIX and the decision id); the second candidate adds the entry and [[link]] and the job proceeds to checks and the verifier.

The second prompt contains '## Sent back', GATE_REASON_PREFIX, 'D02 (README.md)' and '[[link]]'; the first prompt has no send-back. findings.summary: The 'fails without the fix' demonstrations for criteria 1 and 2 only show a compile failure, not the behavioural failure.
findings.evidence: Athena's revert runs exited 101 on unresolved imports (GOVERNING_HEADING, send_back_text_full), not on the count assertions. From the code, the base would run the producer once and fail at check_and_verify, so the assertions would fail, but no run showed it.

summary: The change does what the request asks. The producer prompt now has a section listing each decision that governs a planned file or deliverable: the decision id, the governed paths, and how to reconcile it (a log entry plus a [[link]] with older = decision, newer = entry). The producer loop also runs the decision gate on the work tree after each report. A change it finds unreconciled gets the one shared send-back, carrying the gate's message word for word. If the change is still unreconciled after that, it leaves the loop, and the existing gate in check_and_verify ends the job with the unchanged message. The message text and GATE_REASON_PREFIX are untouched; the wording only moved into one helper, decision_gate. I ran all the new and existing gate, retry, send-back and decision_links tests and they pass. fmt, clippy and the full test suite are cited from Athena's recorded CI results. One environment note: in this snapshot's shared target directory, `cargo test -p athena-core` first failed to compile because a stale athena-data library was cached there (the source is correct). I reran the tests with `--target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, which builds into a fresh subdirectory of the same Athena-set target directory, and everything passed. This is about the build cache, not the candidate. Every changed file is on the expected-deliverables list.
